name: sm-00-data-collection
title: Surrogate data collection — broad observable transition-dataset from baseline rollouts
claim:
An 8-seed ensemble of baseline rollouts can be flattened into a single
pbg-torch TransitionDataset spanning a broad observable panel (growth/mass,
exchange fluxes, metabolic fluxes, protein and transcript abundance,
chromosome state) — ~11.5k observables per step — suitable for training a
neural-network surrogate.
question:
Can the deeply-nested baseline state (pint Quantities, per-agent keys,
dict-valued exchange fluxes, high-dimensional count/flux vectors) be extracted
into a stable, flat (state_t, state_t+1) transition dataset covering every
observable category?

report.title: sm-00-data-collection — broad transition dataset
report.evidence_quality: 8 seeds x 250 steps = 2000 transitions x 11569 observables
report.objective:
Build the training corpus for the surrogate: roll out the v2ecoli baseline
for 8 seeds, stepping one simulated second at a time, and extract a flat
observable vector before and after each step. The PanelLayout (code/observables.py)
discovers a stable column ordering across six observable groups and handles
pint magnitudes, the single-agent key, and the dict-valued exchange fluxes.
report.setup:
code/sample_baseline.py builds the baseline composite per seed (shared ParCa
cache), steps it, and assembles a pbg_torch.TransitionDataset. Trajectories
halt at division (the single-agent assumption breaks once daughters appear).
report.result:
Dataset: 2000 transitions x 11569 observables from 8 trajectories.
Group dimensionality:
  mass=7, exchange=87, base_flux=2820, monomer=4309, mrna=4345, chromosome=1.
All six target groups captured; every step yields a finite flat vector.
report.interpretation:
The broad panel spans all the requested categories. Slowly-varying groups
(mass, counts) and fast/erratic groups (metabolic fluxes) are both present,
which sets up sm-01 to measure where a surrogate is trustworthy.
report.decision: PASS — the transition dataset is built and feeds sm-01.

embed_visualizations.description: Log-scale group-dimensionality bar (11,569 observables across 6 groups: mass, exchange, base_flux, monomer, mrna, chromosome) + per-seed cell_mass and instantaneous_growth_rate trajectories across the 8 sampled seeds. Demonstrates broad coverage and that every extracted value is finite — the corpus that trains the surrogate.

falsifiability:
Fails if any target group is missing from the extracted vector, if extraction
produces non-finite values, or if the per-agent key handling breaks before
division.
